key_insight: Logarithmic qubit encoding is not enough for practical quantum modal analysis: deflation accuracy, circuit expressibility, and measurement costs remain critical.
engineering_relevance: The framework evaluates variational quantum eigensolvers for structural vibration modes and damage localization while preserving mass orthogonality.
method: Use Cholesky whitening to map the generalized eigenproblem to a symmetric Hamiltonian.
Derive a necessary-and-sufficient deflation threshold and bound approximate-projector errors.
Evaluate mapping, ansatz expressibility, preprocessing, Pauli growth, and finite-shot uncertainty separately.
evidence_signal: For 128-DOF chains, whitening increased Pauli terms from 576 to 2,950; first-mode frequency RMS error was 2.45% at 100,000 shots per term, and an oracle-state study localized 10% stiffness loss in 84.5% of trials.
watch_item: Dense transformed operators and costly measurements can offset compact encoding; oracle-state localization does not establish end-to-end hardware performance, and no speedup is claimed.
paper_title: Qubits Are Not Enough: Deflation and Measurement Limits in Variational Quantum Modal Analysis
